triggering_machine_finding.root_cause: ANSI_SENSITIVE_HUMAN_OUTPUT_PARSER — GitHub Actions' vitest output interleaves ANSI color escape codes directly around/inside the summary tokens (e.g. \x1b[1m\x1b[32m4 passed\x1b[39m\x1b[22m); this repository's own local runs (piped to a file, no TTY) never produce this decoration, so the original /\b4 passed\b/ regex matched locally but not in the GitHub Actions runner environment.

A_M2_TEST_RESULT_PORTABILITY.requirement: Normalize terminal decoration (ANSI CSI color/style escapes) before interpreting the Vitest summary. No new dependency — a small deterministic stripAnsi() + order/decoration-agnostic per-line count parser. Must still require exactly: test files total=1/passed=1/failed=0/skipped=0, tests total=4/passed=4/failed=0/skipped=0. Must accept plain local output AND GitHub-ANSI-decorated output. Must reject 0 files, 2 files, 3/4 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped. NO_COLOR alone is explicitly rejected as a sufficient fix — portability must live in the parser itself.
A_M2_TEST_RESULT_PORTABILITY.implemented_as: stripAnsi(), parseSummaryLine(), parseVitestSummary(), isExactM2Result() in scripts/m2-disposable-pg-bootstrap.ts

B_M2_F2_MECHANICAL_MIGRATION_PROOF.requirement: Remove the unconditional record('MAIN:0061-APPLIED', true) supported only by migrate.status===0. Mechanically derive EXPECTED_MIGRATION_COUNT from the canonical Drizzle migration corpus (db/migrations/meta/_journal.json), require the actual drizzle.__drizzle_migrations journal count to equal it, and mechanically establish that migration 0061 is represented via Drizzle 0.45.2's own hashing semantics (sha256 of each migration .sql file's content, one row per applied migration in drizzle.__drizzle_migrations.hash — read directly from drizzle-orm/migrator.js's readMigrationFiles and drizzle-orm/pg-core/dialect.js's PgDialect.migrate, not guessed). Add a deliberate negative/mutation control proving the migration-proof logic can return FAIL.
